text:
Maya: Quick non-work poll  what's the weirdest souvenir you've ever brought home? No judgment, just curious. :globe_with_meridians:
Evan: I have a tiny painted toilet from a roadside shop in Taiwan. It's now a ring holder. :toilet:
Jules: Bought a jar of pickled herring in Norway and carried it on the plane. Smelled like victory at customs. :nauseated_face:
Sam: A taxidermy mouse dressed as a tiny pirate. My partner was not pleased. :skull_and_crossbones:
Maya: Wait that's a whole aesthetic. Pics? :eyes:
Jules: Sadly confiscated by customs at the time. But I have a postcard with the store name.
Evan: Photo of the toilet ring-holder: <https://imgur.com/placeholder_toilet.jpg|toilet-ring.jpg>
Sam: I still have the pirate mouse on a shelf. He occasionally gets dressed up for holidays.
Maya: @kudos-bot cc: for "Most Unusual Souvenir" award? :trophy:
kudos-bot: Award given to Sam: "Most Dramatic Souvenir" :confetti_ball:
Evan: Other honorable mention: a single rubber duck from a river cleanup festival. I refuse to explain how I won it.
Jules: Also once brought back a tiny stone carved like a foot from an island market. No explanation either.
Maya: Love this. New travel rule: only bring home things you can justify in a sent Slack thread.
Sam: Agreed. Also, mandatory pirate-mouse tour when we're back in office.
Maya: Party plan noted. Thanks for sharing, everyone! :sparkles:
